肌.meaning: An astronaut brings home a <part>table</part> from the <part>moon</part>, carved out of moon rock. Everyone who touches it pulls a face: it's dusty, cratered and bumpy as orange peel. Party guests can't stop rubbing its strange <kanji>texture</kanji>.
肌.on: One guest drops her house <sound>key</sound> into a crater on the tabletop.
肌.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the astronaut, rubbing his cheek on it. 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>! Rough as my skin.'

罪.meaning: Grandma counts the fish in her <part>net</part>: one short. Under the table, the dog won't look her in the eye, and a <part>fishbone</part> is stuck in his whiskers. He tries to whistle. His whole face is <kanji>guilt</kanji>.
罪.on: To distract her, he bangs out a cheerful tune on a <sound>xy</sound>lophone.
罪.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and the bone pings onto her plate. '<sound>Me</sound>? Never,' says his face.

謝.meaning: At the village fair, an archer means to <part>shoot</part> an apple off a dummy but pops the mayor's balloon hat instead. He drops his bow, unrolls a long <part>speech</part> on a scroll and reads every page on his knees. All he wants is to <kanji>apologize</kanji>.
謝.on: The mayor forgives him, then bats a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock at his hat just to be even.
謝.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sighs, and knits the mayor a new hat from <sound>ya</sound>rn, the way his <sound>Ma</sound> taught him.

枚.meaning: On a hot day, a <part>tree</part> peels off a thin strip of its bark and folds it into a <part>fan</part>. It works so well that it peels another, and another, stacking them neatly on the grass like paper. Then it counts them: one <kanji>sheet of</kanji> bark, two, three.
枚.on: A crowd of <sound>mi</sound>ce sneaks off with a sheet each, to use as a blanket.

抱.meaning: A sailor tries to <part>pack up</part> his ship's <part>anchor</part> in a suitcase, but it won't fit, so he wraps both arms round it and carries it home on the bus. At the door his mum wraps both arms round him, anchor and all. A double <kanji>embrace</kanji>.
抱.on: Then she sprays the salty anchor clean with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
抱.kun: 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!' he beams, and hugs the dripping anchor once more.

序.meaning: A garden <part>shed</part> hosts a snail race. <part>Beforehand</part>, a beetle in a bow tie reads out a long introduction about the history of snails, the weather and his own childhood. The snails fall asleep before the start. Nobody remembers the race, only the <kanji>preface</kanji>.
序.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger runs past the shed and laps the sleeping snails twice.
序.kun: The beetle sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', then adds, '<sound>Ee</sound>, by the way...', and starts a second speech.

麦.meaning: A farmer watches the weather report in the middle of his field, on a TV with a tall <part>TV antenna</part>, sitting in a <part>folding chair</part>. One summer the stalks grow so high they wrap round the antenna, and every channel shows nothing but golden, whiskery heads of <kanji>barley</kanji>.
麦.on: He loosens his belt <sound>buck</sound>le after a third bowl of soup made from it.
麦.kun: Behind his chair, a <sound>moo</sound>se and two <sound>gee</sound>se munch the stalks.
